statuses.name: Discussed
statuses.hint: The people concerned have talked it through.

statuses.name: Agreed
statuses.hint: Those whose action it needs have said yes.

statuses.name: Funded
statuses.hint: The money is committed, for as long as it is needed.

statuses.name: Operating
statuses.hint: It is working on the ground.

statuses.name: Reviewed
statuses.hint: Checked with the people it serves, and improved.

principles.name: Work through those who hold the mandate
principles.text: Protection is delivered by the bodies already responsible for it. The coordinator helps them agree; it does not take their place.

principles.name: Invite, never instruct
principles.text: Every commitment is voluntary until it is agreed, and recorded as such.

principles.name: Describe gaps as shared problems
principles.text: A missing piece is a task to solve together, never a fault to assign.

principles.name: Include the people affected, with consent
principles.text: Workers and their representatives shape the plan. Personal details are kept private and used only with permission.

principles.name: Use official channels
principles.text: Alerts, complaints and disagreements go through the channels set up for them. When views differ, pause, record and refer to the body with the mandate.

principles.name: Be open about the coordinator’s role
principles.text: Say who funds the coordination, what the coordinator does itself, and what it does not decide.

capabilities.name: Understand local risk
capabilities.does: Combine heat evidence with work, housing, health and service conditions.

capabilities.name: Understand who decides what
capabilities.does: Find who holds authority, who pays, who carries the cost and who is missing.
capabilities.output: A map of mandates and open decisions

capabilities.name: Help agreements form
capabilities.does: Work out responsibilities, contributions and what happens when something fails.

capabilities.name: Prepare delivery and money
capabilities.does: Cost what would be built and what would keep it running; find suitable funding.

capabilities.name: Support the season
capabilities.does: Check readiness, notice failures and connect the people who can fix them.

capabilities.name: Learn and make it last
capabilities.does: Test what reached people, and carry improvements into budgets and procedures.

missing: Women who trade or work at night
Older workers and people with health conditions
Children who come to work with a parent
feedback: Choose how people can raise a problem
Through their association or union representative
A local helpline with a named person who answers
A suggestion box and a weekly visit
A short meeting at the start of each hot week
survive: The running cost is in an annual budget
It is written into a procedure, rule or contract
A named post, not a person, is responsible
A review date after each hot season is fixed
checks: Was safe water reliably there when it was needed?
Did the service keep working through the whole season?
Could workers actually stop and rest when it was hottest?
Did help with money arrive before the hardest days?
Did anything change the next season because of them?
note: Every place, person and organisation here is hypothetical, a composite drawn from common situations. Amounts are illustrative. The simulation adds up hours and pay; it does not predict illness.

evidence.text: UNDRR’s work on extreme heat links resilience to coordination across sectors, financing and sustained action over different time horizons.
In Bangladesh, heat response depends on many agencies at once: health, labour, city authorities, utilities and humanitarian partners.

source.label: Rockefeller Foundation: who owns the response to heat in Bangladesh?

evidence.text: Ahmedabad’s heat action plan brought city departments, hospitals and community groups together around shared alerts and actions.

source.label: NRDC on Ahmedabad’s heat action plan

evidence.text: Social protection can cushion the income workers lose to extreme heat, if it is designed to arrive in time.

source.label: ILO: addressing the impacts of extreme heat through social protection

evidence.text: WHO’s guidance on heat–health action plans sets out the elements a plan needs, from early warning to evaluation.

scenarios.name: The wholesale market
scenarios.where: A wholesale vegetable market in a mid-sized city in South Asia
scenarios.boundary: The market yard, its lanes and its loading bays, from the 4 am arrivals to the afternoon clean-up.
scenarios.task: Help vendors, loaders and sanitation workers reach water, rest and help with money during dangerous heat, while the market keeps working.
outside: Heat warnings from the national weather service
State and national social protection schemes

people.name: Meena
people.day: Arrives at 4 am to buy from wholesalers and sells from a stall under a tarpaulin until her stock is gone.
people.heat: By noon the tarpaulin traps the heat. Buyers stop coming and leafy greens wilt.

people.name: Raju
people.day: Paid by the load, carrying sacks from the trucks to the stalls. The busiest hours are 5 to 11 am.
people.heat: Late trucks mean carrying 40 kg sacks in the worst heat, and stopping means losing loads to others.

people.name: Lakshmi
people.day: Employed by a contractor to sweep the yard and clear waste after trading ends, from 1 pm.
people.heat: Her shift starts as the heat peaks, and she cannot leave the yard to find water.
people.lossNote: Her pay is fixed; heat costs her health, not wages.

actors.name: Market committee
actors.general: Runs the market: its hours, its layout and who trades where.

actors.name: Municipal corporation
actors.general: Water connections, toilets, lighting, sanitation contracts and public health.

actors.name: Water utility or tanker operator
actors.general: Supplies and tests drinking water.

actors.name: Traders’ association
actors.general: Speaks for stall holders and wholesalers, and arranges with transporters.

actors.name: Loaders’ association
actors.general: Speaks for head-load workers and agrees rates with traders.

actors.name: Sanitation contractor
actors.general: Employs the cleaning staff and sets their shifts.

actors.name: Nearby primary health centre
actors.general: First aid and treatment for heat illness.

actors.name: District disaster management office
actors.general: Issues local heat alerts and coordinates the official response.

actors.name: A state scheme or donor
actors.general: Can hold money for payments released on a forecast.

actors.name: Coordinating organisation (you)
actors.general: Convenes the others, keeps the record and follows up. Holds no authority of its own.

measures.name: A shaded rest point with water
measures.does: A shaded corner of the yard with benches, drinking water and oral rehydration salts.
measures.line: rests in the shade and drinks clean water

reqs.text: A site in the yard, where workers actually pass
reqs.fail: There is no agreed site, so the rest point never opens.

reqs.text: A named person opens it early, cleans it and restocks the salts
reqs.fail: Nobody opens the rest point before 10 am, after the worst loading hours.

reqs.text: Safe water, tested and refilled every day
reqs.fail: Nobody agreed who refills the water; by now the cans are empty.

reqs.text: Running costs paid for the whole hot season
reqs.fail: The money covered the opening, not the season; the salts have run out.

measures.name: Earlier market hours on alert days
measures.does: On an official heat alert, trading and loading start an hour earlier, and the heaviest unloading ends by 11 am.

reqs.text: The market committee changes the hours on alert days
reqs.fail: The hours never changed: nobody was able to decide on the day.

reqs.text: Wholesalers ask transporters to arrive earlier
reqs.fail: Trucks still arrive at noon, so loading stays in the hottest hours.

reqs.text: The alert reaches the market by the evening before
reqs.fail: The alert arrived at 9 am, after the market had opened as usual.

measures.name: Breaks that keep a loader’s place
measures.does: Traders and loaders agree that a break in the hottest hours does not lose a worker his place in the queue.
measures.line: takes a break without losing his place

reqs.text: A written understanding between traders and loaders
reqs.fail: Without an understanding, a loader who rests loses his turn, so nobody rests.

reqs.text: Loaders’ representatives helped shape it
reqs.fail: The arrangement was made without the loaders, and few rely on it.

measures.name: Cleaning moved to the cooler evening
measures.does: On alert days, cleaning starts at 5 pm instead of 1 pm, with the same pay.
measures.line: cleans in the cooler evening, for the same pay

reqs.text: The city allows the contractor to change shift times
reqs.fail: The contract fixes the shift at 1 pm, so it cannot move.

reqs.text: The contractor changes the roster and keeps pay the same
reqs.fail: The roster was never changed.

reqs.text: Lights in the yard for evening work
reqs.fail: Without lights, evening cleaning is not safe, so the shift stays at 1 pm.

measures.name: Cash before the heatwave
measures.does: A small payment released on the heat forecast to registered vendors and loaders, before the hottest days.
measures.line: has cash in hand before the hottest days

reqs.text: A list of who is eligible, made with the associations and with consent
reqs.fail: There was no agreed list, so payment waited.

reqs.text: Money set aside before the season
reqs.fail: The money was not set aside in advance, so nothing could be released.

reqs.text: An agreed forecast trigger that releases it
reqs.fail: Without an agreed trigger, the payment moved only after the heatwave.

measures.name: First-aiders and a clinic link
measures.does: Two trained first-aiders in the market and a direct line to the health centre.
measures.line: knows a first-aider is minutes away

reqs.text: Two market workers trained in heat first aid
reqs.fail: Nobody in the market has been trained.

reqs.text: The health centre agrees to take calls and send help
reqs.fail: There is no agreed line to the health centre.

scenarios.name: The garment workshops
scenarios.where: A cluster of small garment workshops on the edge of a city in Southeast Asia
scenarios.boundary: Twelve workshops along two lanes, the shared water point and the road where the trucks load.
scenarios.task: Keep the workshops cool enough to work safely, and let workers rest in the worst heat without losing pay.
outside: Orders and deadlines set by buying companies

people.name: Dara
people.day: Sews collars, paid by the piece, under a metal roof with one fan for six machines.
people.heat: After lunch the room passes 38 °C. Her hands slow, and so does her pay.

people.name: Sokha
people.day: Presses finished garments beside steam irons all day.
people.heat: The irons add their own heat to the hot season. Dizziness is common by mid-afternoon.

people.name: Vuthy
people.day: Carries bundles to the trucks and rides deliveries across the city.
people.heat: Loading happens in the open yard at noon, when the trucks come.

actors.name: Workshop owners’ group
actors.general: Set hours, breaks and conditions inside the workshops.

actors.name: Local authority
actors.general: Shared water point, roads, building permissions and local public health.

actors.name: Labour inspection office
actors.general: Advises on and inspects workplace conditions.

actors.name: Electricity utility
actors.general: Supply and reliability for fans and cooling.

actors.name: Workers’ representatives
actors.general: Speak for workers in each workshop.

actors.name: Health centre
actors.general: Treatment for heat illness.

actors.name: Companies placing orders
actors.general: Set order volumes and deadlines; some support workplace improvements.

actors.name: Coordinating organisation (you)
actors.general: Convenes the others, keeps the record and follows up. Holds no authority of its own.

measures.name: Cool roofs and better airflow
measures.does: A reflective coating on the metal roofs, roof vents and enough working fans.

reqs.text: Building owners allow the coating and vents
reqs.fail: The building owners never agreed, so the roofs stayed bare.

reqs.text: The cost is shared and paid
reqs.fail: Nobody agreed to pay, so the work never started.

reqs.text: Power is reliable enough to run the fans
reqs.fail: Afternoon power cuts stop the fans just when they matter.

measures.name: Paid heat breaks
measures.does: Ten-minute breaks every hour when the workshop passes an agreed temperature, without losing piece pay.
measures.line: takes paid breaks in the hottest hours

reqs.text: Owners agree the break rule and how piece pay is protected
reqs.fail: Breaks cost piece pay, so almost nobody takes them.

reqs.text: Workers’ representatives helped set the temperature and the rule
reqs.fail: The rule was set without the workers, and few rely on it.

reqs.text: A thermometer in each workshop, read by a named person
reqs.fail: Nobody reads the thermometer, so the break rule never starts.

reqs.text: Order deadlines leave room for breaks in the hot season
reqs.fail: A rush order arrives; breaks are dropped to meet the deadline.

measures.name: Cool drinking water on every floor
measures.does: Filtered water dispensers on each floor, refilled daily.
measures.line: drinks cool water without leaving the floor

reqs.text: The shared water point supplies enough clean water
reqs.fail: The shared water point runs dry in the afternoons.

reqs.text: A named person refills and cleans the dispensers
reqs.fail: Nobody refills the dispensers after the first day.

measures.name: Loading moved out of midday
measures.does: Trucks load before 10 am or after 4 pm on hot days.

reqs.text: Owners and transporters agree the loading times
reqs.fail: The trucks still arrive at noon.

reqs.text: The local authority allows early and late loading on the lane
reqs.fail: Loading outside daytime hours is not allowed on the lane.

measures.name: A clinic link and first aid
measures.does: A first-aid kit and a trained person in each workshop, and a direct line to the health centre.
measures.line: knows a first-aider is close by

reqs.text: One trained first-aider in each workshop
reqs.fail: Nobody has been trained.

reqs.text: The health centre agrees a direct line
reqs.fail: There is no agreed line to the health centre.

scenarios.name: The village at harvest
scenarios.where: A farming village in a river delta in South Asia, at harvest time
scenarios.boundary: The village, its fields and its two water points, during the three weeks of harvest.
scenarios.task: Help farm workers and households get through harvest heat with water, rest and money, without losing the crop.
outside: National social protection and insurance schemes

people.name: Rina
people.day: Cuts and bundles rice for a daily wage, from 7 am until the landowner says stop.
people.heat: The fields have no shade. Working into the afternoon is the price of a full day’s wage.

people.name: Kalam
people.day: Farms his own small plot and hires two labourers at harvest.
people.heat: If the harvest slows in the heat, the crop is at risk from early rain; he works through the worst hours.

people.name: Shila
people.role: Fetches water and cares for the family
people.day: Walks to the water point twice a day and cares for her children and her mother-in-law.
people.heat: The nearer handpump is broken, so the walk is long, and it falls in the hottest part of the day.
people.lossNote: Her work is unpaid; heat costs her health and time.

actors.name: Village council
actors.general: Local decisions, small works and a link to district schemes.

actors.name: Farmers’ group
actors.general: Landowners and smallholders who hire labour and set working hours.

actors.name: Labourers’ group
actors.general: Speaks for daily-wage farm workers.

actors.name: Water committee
actors.general: Looks after the handpumps and water points.

actors.name: Community health worker
actors.general: Home visits, first aid and referral to the health post.

actors.name: District office
actors.general: Passes on heat alerts and can release scheme funds.

actors.name: A state scheme or donor
actors.general: Can hold money for payments released on a forecast.

actors.name: Coordinating organisation (you)
actors.general: Convenes the others, keeps the record and follows up. Holds no authority of its own.

measures.name: Harvest in the cool hours
measures.does: On alert days, harvesting runs from 5 to 10 am and again from 4 pm, for a full day’s wage.
measures.line: harvests in the cooler hours for a full wage

reqs.text: Farmers agree the hours and the full day’s wage
reqs.fail: Farmers kept the usual hours; a shorter day would cost a day’s wage.

reqs.text: The labourers’ group helped set the arrangement
reqs.fail: The labourers were not part of it, and few took it up.

reqs.text: The alert reaches the village the evening before
reqs.fail: The alert arrived after work had started.

measures.name: The near handpump repaired
measures.does: The broken handpump fixed, with a shaded waiting place.
measures.line: fetches water from the near pump, in the shade

reqs.text: The water committee repairs the pump
reqs.fail: The pump is still broken.

reqs.text: Money for parts and upkeep
reqs.fail: No money for parts, so the repair waits.

reqs.text: The water is tested as safe to drink
reqs.fail: The water was never tested, and families stop trusting it.

measures.name: Shade and water at the field edge
measures.does: A movable shade cloth and water cans where people work.
measures.line: rests in the shade at the field edge

reqs.text: Farmers provide shade and water at the field
reqs.fail: There is still no shade at the field.

reqs.text: Someone refills the cans at midday
reqs.fail: The cans are empty by noon.

measures.name: Health worker heat rounds
measures.does: Daily visits to older people and families with infants on alert days, with salts and advice.
measures.line: is visited by the health worker

reqs.text: A list of households to visit, made with consent
reqs.fail: There was no list, so the visits did not reach the right homes.

reqs.text: The health worker’s time is freed for rounds
reqs.fail: The health worker’s other duties left no time for rounds.

measures.name: Cash before the hottest days
measures.does: A small payment on the heat forecast to labourer households.
measures.line: has cash in hand before the hottest days

reqs.text: A list of eligible households, made with consent
reqs.fail: There was no agreed list, so payment waited.

reqs.text: Money set aside before harvest
reqs.fail: The money was not set aside in advance.

reqs.text: An agreed forecast trigger that releases it
reqs.fail: Without an agreed trigger, the payment arrived after harvest.
